    THE FRAMEFIX MODEL

    A useful estimate.
    Not a fake benchmark.

    FrameFix combines relative CPU and GPU performance, a game-specific workload profile, resolution scaling and memory pressure. It returns a range because no two PCs run exactly alike.

    01

    Normalize the hardware

    Parts are compared using practical relative performance scores.

    02

    Apply the game profile

    CPU-heavy and GPU-heavy games scale differently.

    03

    Recommend, don’t promise

    The model favors stable targets over unrealistic peak numbers.

    QUICK ANSWERS

    FPS calculator FAQ

    How accurate are the estimates?

    Use them as a planning range, not a guaranteed benchmark. Game updates, temperatures, drivers, overclocks and background tasks can move the result.

    Does more RAM always increase FPS?

    No. Enough RAM prevents stutter and slowdowns, but extra capacity above a game’s needs rarely adds meaningful average FPS.

    What does “bottleneck” mean?

    It is the component most likely to limit performance in the selected game and resolution. Every PC has a limiting part; the goal is a sensible balance.

    Does FrameFix include ray tracing?

    Not in this first model. Results assume standard rasterized graphics unless a game profile explicitly says otherwise.
